blocks.text: Bogotá – Medellín – El Peñón and Guatapé

Meet in the hotel lobby at the appointed time, then transfer to the airport for your flight to Medellín. An English-speaking guide will meet you on arrival. From there, continue towards Guatapé and El Peñol.

El Peñón de Guatapé lies between the towns of El Peñol and Guatapé. Both towns claim it as their landmark, so its name brings the two names together.

The Tahamí people lived in this area. They considered the rock sacred and called it “mujarra”, meaning “stone”. One local legend tells of a fish named Batolito that leapt out of the sea to protect people from the wrath of the gods of the sky. During the battle it turned to stone, becoming El Peñón de Guatapé.

The rock rises alone above the low hills. It stands about 220 metres high, with roughly two thirds of the rock still underground. It is estimated to be more than 70 million years old. It has been protected by the state since the 1940s. The first ascent took place in 1954 and lasted five days.

As you climb, views open up over the hills, the water and the many islands. You can try fruit beer at the entrance to the rock.

Afterwards, you will visit Guatapé. The village is known for its brightly coloured façades, with reliefs depicting scenes from everyday life along the lower walls of the houses. There will be time for a coffee and a walk through the streets.

Return to Medellín to check in at your hotel and rest.
